input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: Section 7.6 imposes liquidated damages payable by us (USD 25,000 per day) for any delay in providing a dependency. This is one-way against Customer, has no cap, no materiality threshold, and no grace or notice mechanic, so it triggers on even minor or brief delays and can quickly exceed the remaining contract value — walk-away territory under this rule. It is not an early-termination fee, so the 3-month fallback is unavailable; nor is it offset by any service credits or Vendor-payable LDs. The exposure also appears to sit outside the liability regime: §§ 21.2 and 21.3 exclude consequential damages and define Excluded Claims but do not cap this agreed-damages obligation. We therefore replace the payment with day-for-day schedule relief for Vendor, which addresses the underlying delay risk without a Customer-payable penalty (preferred position).

ops.oldText: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: 7.6 If Customer delays in providing a dependency, Vendor's sole remedy is a day-for-day extension of the affected schedule or milestone dates, and Customer shall not be liable for liquidated damages or any other penalty for that delay.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, so we have replaced the USD 25,000 per day charge with day-for-day schedule relief for Vendor, which addresses the delay without an uncapped penalty. Our playbook position is no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.
proposal.summary: Replace Customer-payable liquidated damages for dependency delay with day-for-day schedule relief.
